title: `first`, `last`: the first and last row in input order, NULL included
verdict: input order, deterministic; NULLs taken unless `ignore_nulls=True`
description: `first` and `last` take the first and last row of the group in input order, also when it is NULL; `ignore_nulls=True` skips NULLs. Over 200 000 rows in 10 groups, in memory and streaming, `first` was the least row index, `last` the greatest, and the list a group collects (`pl.col(x)` in `agg`, `implode`) kept input order.
`str.join` concatenates in that order and skips NULLs.

Streaming, `first` and `last` are reductions keyed by the morsel's sequence number: `first` keeps the value of the lowest sequence number (the first row of a morsel, or the earliest row of a group in it), `last` the highest (a later row of the same morsel replaces it), and pipelines merge by the same rule. So they follow input order as far as morsel numbers do. `implode` with `maintain_order` (the list `agg(pl.col(x))` builds) has no streaming lowering: a group_by with it falls back to the in-memory engine, and ungrouped it runs in the in-memory fallback. `implode(maintain_order=False)` streams and keeps no order.
reference: `tie_pick`: any row of the group (each measure may take its own); `tie_order`: any order for `string_agg` and `array_agg`. Polars's choice is allowed, and deterministic where DuckDB's depends on parallelism (duckdb-mode-ties).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `First::should_replace` keeps the lowest sequence id, `Last` the highest (`new >= old`)
`combine`, `reduce_one`, `reduce_ca` by sequence id; `reduce_ca` takes the morsel's first or last value
grouped: `Implode { maintain_order: true }` does not (the group_by falls back)

`test_streaming_group_by_first_last_stored`, `engine='streaming'` with morsels of 32, hot tables of 4 and stored partitions: over `k = i % 50`, `v = i if i >= 50 else NULL`, `first` is NULL, `last` 950 + k, `first(ignore_nulls=True)` 50 + k, `last(ignore_nulls=True)` 950 + k
`test_streaming_group_by_types`, streaming: `first` and `last` of strings, booleans and dates follow input order within the group

notes: Pins on the streaming engine that `first` and `last` take the group's first and last row in input order, NULL included, across morsels and partitions.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.
Streaming agrees with memory: over 100 000 rows in 7 groups, `first` and `last` are the group's least and greatest row index, and the list `agg(pl.col('i'))` builds is in input order.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
